contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

Using the map of potential fiber segments and their installation prices, pick which segments to lay so that every marked community center is linked by a connected network while keeping the total installation price as low as possible and allowing intermediate junctions where helpful.

Decide which garden paths to build between existing stepping stones so that all flagged seating areas are reachable from each other along the built paths, using other stepping stones as intermediate points if needed, and minimizing the total path length.

Choose a subset of overhead cable routes from the set of feasible spans so that every designated distribution box is linked into a connected line, using available poles as relay points when useful, and minimize the sum of span lengths.

Select corridor segments to open within the gallery blueprint so that all highlighted exhibit rooms are connected by an uninterrupted route, optionally passing through other galleries, while keeping the total length of opened corridors as small as possible.

Pick irrigation channel sections to construct on the farm grid so that each marked crop plot has a water connection within a contiguous network, allowing water nodes at field corners to be used, and minimizing total length of channels constructed.

Decide which temporary walkways to lay across the park so that all vendor booths indicated on the plan are interconnected via the installed walkways, using existing plazas as intermediate junctions if helpful, and keep aggregate walkway length minimal.

From the set of available conduit runs between poles and panels, choose which conduits to install so that each required service panel is tied into a continuous electrical path, permitting extra junction boxes, and minimize the overall installation cost.

Pick which trail links to maintain on the forest map so that all marked viewpoints become part of a connected trail network, optionally using intermediate clearings, while minimizing the total maintenance distance.

Choose which sidewalks to repair so that every designated school entrance is connected to the repaired sidewalk network, possibly routing through other intersections, while minimizing the total repair expense.

Select routes inside the warehouse to keep clear so that all priority storage bays are reachable within a connected corridor system, using other aisles as links if necessary, and minimize the total length of cleared routes.

Determine which footbridges and boardwalk segments to restore so that all important marsh observation points are connected by continuous passage, allowing restoration of intermediate platforms, and minimize total repair cost.

Decide which campus backbone fiber links to activate so that the set of key academic buildings are all connected through the active network, using other building interconnects as intermediate hops, and keep total activated cable length as low as possible.

Choose which delivery lanes between stores to keep open so that every flagship location is connected within a delivery network, allowing stopovers at regional hubs, while minimizing total travel distance of the network.

From available pipeline segments, select which ones to install so that all specified treatment sites are linked in a connected pipeline system, permitting junction nodes at existing valve stations, and minimize total pipeline length.
Pick which decorative lighting runs to wire so that all landmark trees are included in a contiguous powered circuit, using lamp posts as connectors where useful, and minimize overall wiring used.

Identify which access roads to keep open in the subdivision so that all hydrant locations remain reachable within the preserved road network, allowing passage through minor streets, and minimize the total length of roads retained.

Select taxiway sections to clear of snow so that all assigned gates are reachable from each other via cleared taxiways, using other aprons as intermediate paths if helpful, and minimize the total cleared distance.

Choose which wildlife corridors to restore so that all protected habitats marked on the map become connected through the restored corridors, permitting stepping stones in unprotected patches, while minimizing restoration area.

Decide which display truss segments to assemble so that all featured installations are connected by an accessible support structure, allowing additional support nodes, and minimize total truss length used.

Pick which decorative fence sections to install between properties so that every agreed garden is part of a continuous fenced network, with the option to link via shared gate posts, and minimize total fencing length.

A city planner asks you to choose a set of streets to trench so that a network of fiber connects all designated municipal buildings while using as little trench length as possible, and you may route through other intersections so that every designated building lies within the same connected network.

A homeowner wants you to pick which pipes to install in the yard so that all marked garden beds receive water while keeping the total pipe length minimal, and you may branch through other points in the garden as needed to ensure all marked beds are linked by a continuous piping system.

A park ranger needs a recommendation for which footpaths to improve so that all trailheads are joined into a single connected trail network with the least total paving length, allowing the route to pass through other clearings or junctions.

A museum curator asks you to decide which wiring runs to install so that every display case is connected to the security loop while minimizing the overall cable length, and you can route cables through other rooms so that all required cases sit on one connected circuit.

A telecom manager requests a plan selecting which office corridors to run data cable through so that every critical workstation is in the same network while minimizing total cable used, with the option to pass wiring through other rooms to create connectivity.

A campsite manager wants guidance on where to place trail markers and cleared paths so that all campsites are connected in a single accessible route with minimal total trail length, and you are allowed to link via other common areas.

A utilities coordinator asks you to pick which distribution lines to build so that all substations are connected in a continuous grid while keeping material cost as low as possible, permitting connection through other junctions.

A school administrator needs a plan identifying which hallways to widen so that all classrooms designated for a program are contiguous via a single accessible corridor system while minimizing total renovation length, and you may use other public spaces as links.

A neighborhood association asks you to choose which lamppost circuits to connect so that all community squares share the same lighting network with the least total wiring, allowing the network to pass through other poles or junction boxes.

A logistics planner needs to determine which rural roads to include so that all pickup locations are connected by a single reachable route network while keeping the summed travel distance minimal, and you may include additional crossroads to form connections.

A building manager wants to pick which HVAC ducts to install so that all required rooms are served by one connected ventilation path while minimizing total duct length, and ducts may pass through other service spaces to link rooms.

A wildlife biologist asks you to decide which corridors to maintain so that all monitored habitats are linked in one contiguous movement network with as little fencing or clearing as possible, and connections may run through intermediate patches.

A retail chain planner requests a layout of which backroom passages to open so that every designated store area is part of one connected service route while minimizing total passage length, and you may use other storage zones to interconnect them.

An event venue director needs you to select platform connectors so that all staging zones form one connected backstage network with the smallest total connector length, and you may route through other backstage areas to join them.

A city parks team asks you to choose which benches and short paths to link so that all picnic groves are connected by one continuous promenade while keeping the overall path length minimal, and intermediate clearings may be used to tie sections together.

A data center operator wants a plan for which fiber trunks to activate so that all critical racks are in one connected fabric while minimizing total active fiber length, and cables may route via other racks or patch points.

A public safety planner asks you to select which sidewalks to keep clear so that all emergency shelters are connected by a single continuous pedestrian route with the least total cleared distance, and you may use side streets and plazas to form links.

A museum exhibit designer needs you to decide which display connectors to install so that all interactive stations are joined into one connected visitor circuit while minimizing the total connector length, and you can link stations through other gallery spaces.

As a city planner, decide which streets to pave so that all neighborhood hubs are linked by a continuous paved network while keeping the total paving length as small as possible, and you may use other intersections as junctions to reduce overall length.

As a festival organizer, choose which walkways to build so that every stage and vendor area is joined in a single connected route network with minimum total construction cost, and you may add temporary link points to lower the expense.

As a network engineer, select fiber cable segments to activate so that all required offices are connected in a continuous network while minimizing the sum of cable lengths, and you may route through intermediate closets to reduce the overall distance.

As a telecom planner, pick microwave link hops to enable so that all cell sites form a connected communication backbone with minimum overall link cost, and you may use relay towers that are not required sites to reduce expense.

As a museum curator, choose which corridors to open so that every exhibit hall is connected within a continuous visitor path while minimizing the total opened corridor length, and you may use intermediate foyers to bridge halls.

As a university planner, select pedestrian bridges and walkways to construct so that all academic buildings are linked in a connected campus network with the smallest possible sum of walkway length, allowing additional plazas to serve as connectors.

As a charging network designer, decide which intercluster links to establish so that every parking cluster is part of a connected charging grid minimizing total cable run cost, and you may include intermediate junction boxes to lower overall cable length.

As a disaster relief coordinator, choose which temporary roads to clear so that all shelters are connected by a usable road network with minimum total cleared distance, and you may clear through additional crossroads to make shorter connections.

As a ski resort manager, select which lifts and connectors to operate so that all lodges and slopes are joined into a continuous access network while minimizing the sum of operational track length, and you may use intermediate transfer points to link sectors.

As a garden designer, pick which hedges and paths to plant so that all seating areas are connected by a continuous green walkway with the least total planting length, and you may include extra garden nodes to create shorter links.

As a campus IT manager, select where to run backbone cables so that all wireless access clusters are connected into a single backbone with minimum total cable distance, and you may use intermediate hardware rooms as connection points.

As a neighborhood lighting designer, choose which lamp posts to interconnect so that all plazas are part of a single illuminated circuit minimizing the sum of wiring length, and you may link through unused poles to shorten runs.

As a marina manager, pick dock segments to retrofit so that all berthing zones are connected by a continuous walkway system while keeping the total retrofit length as low as possible, and you may use spare piers as intermediate connectors.

As a volunteer coordinator, decide which footpaths to repair so that all donation drop points are connected within a single walkable network minimizing total repair distance, and you may repair through other junctions to reduce the total.
