global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of existing stepping stones in the courtyard; each stone represents a node where paths can start, end, or pass through.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate straight path segments between pairs of stepping stones that could be built (each corresponds to an edge the planner may choose to lay).

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of stepping stone identifiers that are flagged seating areas; these stones must be connected to each other by the chosen built paths (other stones may be used as intermediates).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint stepping stone for this candidate path segment (one end of the potential path to construct).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint stepping stone for this candidate path segment (the opposite end of the potential path to construct).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Physical length of this candidate path segment between the two stepping stones, representing the cost (amount of path to lay) if this segment is chosen.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of nodes in the instance: counts every utility pole and every fixed distribution box that can appear as an endpoint for cable. Node IDs referenced below (u, v, terminals) use this indexing.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of feasible overhead spans (candidate edges) available to string cable between nodes. Equals the number of span entries provided (each with u, v, w).

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node IDs corresponding to the distribution boxes that must be connected into a single continuous overhead line. These are the terminals that the selected spans must span (non-terminal poles may be used as relays).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Node ID of one endpoint of this candidate overhead span; may be a pole or a distribution box. Matches the node indexing given by total_poles_and_boxes and referenced in required_distribution_boxes.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Node ID of the other endpoint of this candidate overhead span; may be a pole or a distribution box. Together with span_endpoint_a defines a feasible span you may choose.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (weight/cost) of this candidate span, in meters (or consistent distance units). If the span is selected in the plan, this value is added to the total cable length objective to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of locations in the gallery blueprint treated as graph nodes — includes individual exhibit rooms and corridor intersections where hallways meet.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of corridor segments in the blueprint treated as graph edges — each segment is a distinct hallway piece that can be opened (counted once if opened).

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to the highlighted exhibit rooms that must all be connected by the unlocked corridor network (every entry must lie on the single continuous route).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location for this corridor segment (a room or corridor intersection node).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location for this corridor segment (the node at the opposite end of the hallway piece).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Physical length (cost) of this corridor segment; used to sum the total length of opened corridors — the objective is to minimize the sum of these lengths while connecting all highlighted rooms.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of junctions in the farm irrigation graph (each junction is a potential water-node at a field corner or other grid intersection). Nodes are referenced by their IDs when specifying edges or terminals.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of possible irrigation channel sections (edge candidates) between junctions in the layout. Each section can be dug (chosen) or left out; its length contributes once to the total digging cost if chosen.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node IDs corresponding to the marked crop plots that must be connected into the single contiguous watering network. These terminals must be spanned by the selected channel sections, using junctions (non-terminal nodes) as needed.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: ID of one endpoint junction for this channel section (a grid corner or node). Together with 'junction_v' it identifies the channel candidate connecting two junctions.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: ID of the other endpoint junction for this channel section (a grid corner or node). The section connects 'junction_u' and 'junction_v' and is either built or not.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Physical length (cost) of digging this channel section, typically measured in the same distance units across the farm. Minimizing the sum of chosen sections' lengths yields the least digging work.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations shown on the plan (this includes all vendor booths and all existing plazas/possible junction points). Use this to know how many nodes exist in the park network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate temporary walkway segments drawn on the plan (each is a possible installation between two locations). This is the count of edges you may choose from when forming the connected network.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of nodes that correspond to vendor booths which must all be connected by the installed walkways. These are the required terminals that cannot be left disconnected; plazas may be used as intermediate junctions but are not required to be all included.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location of a candidate walkway segment (a node id referring to either a vendor booth or an existing plaza) as shown on the plan.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location of the same candidate walkway segment (a node id referring to either a vendor booth or an existing plaza). Together with 'endpoint_a' this defines which two spots the possible walkway would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Physical length (cost) of the candidate walkway segment between the two endpoints, in the units given on the plan (e.g., meters). The sum of chosen segments' lengths is the total installed walkway length to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct graph vertices representing physical locations on the site map — this includes poles, service panels, and any pre-mapped positions where junction boxes or intermediate connection points may sit. Solver uses this to know how many nodes are indexed in the conduit network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of available conduit run options (graph edges) listed in the map. Each corresponds to a possible conduit installation between two locations; the solver will choose a subset of these to build.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of node identifiers that are required service panels which must be connected into one continuous electrical path. These are the terminals that cannot be left disconnected; other nodes may be used as intermediate (Steiner) points.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location identifier for this available conduit run. Matches a node index/name from the site map (pole, panel, or junction point).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location identifier for this available conduit run. Together with 'endpoint_a' it defines which two locations the conduit would connect if chosen.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The installation cost (weight) for this conduit run between endpoint_a and endpoint_b — usually in dollars and including material and labor. The solver minimizes the sum of chosen run_cost values while ensuring all required_service_panels are connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the forest map (every viewpoint plus every intermediate clearing). This is the count of nodes available when choosing which trail links to keep for the maintenance route.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of trail segments shown on the map. Each segment is a candidate piece of trail that can be kept (maintained) and contributes its length to the total maintenance distance if chosen.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers that correspond to the flagged viewpoints which must all be connected by the retained trail network. Non-listed nodes are clearings that may be used as intermediate Steiner nodes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location for a particular trail segment (a node index or label). This, together with 'v', names the two locations the segment connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location for that trail segment (a node index or label). The segment runs between 'trail_endpoint_a' and 'trail_endpoint_b'.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Physical length (maintenance distance) of the trail segment between the two endpoints. When a segment is included in the plan it adds this length once toward the total distance to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of street intersections and sidewalk endpoints in the map (every graph node). This counts all nodes available for use when planning repairs, including designated school entrances and potential intermediate intersections (Steiner nodes).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of sidewalk segments considered for repair (graph edges). Each entry corresponds to a specific sidewalk piece between two intersections that can be repaired at the listed cost.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers that are the designated school entrances which must be connected by the repaired sidewalk network. Every listed entrance must be reachable through chosen repaired segments; other intersections may be repaired to join them.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint intersection for this sidewalk segment. Used together with 'endpoint_b' to specify which two intersections the sidewalk connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint intersection for this sidewalk segment. The pair (endpoint_a, endpoint_b) defines the specific sidewalk piece that can be repaired.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary cost to repair this particular sidewalk segment (edge weight). When chosen in the plan this amount is added once to the total repair expense for the network.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct nodes in the warehouse graph — each node represents an aisle intersection, corridor endpoint, or a bay access point used for routing between storage bays.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct aisle segments (corridor stretches) that connect pairs of nodes. Each edge corresponds to a physical aisle that could be cleared and is counted once.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to the priority storage bays that must be reachable. These terminal nodes must all be connected within the cleared corridor system.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint node for this aisle segment (e.g., an intersection or bay access). Used with 'aisle_endpoint_v' to specify which two nodes the segment links.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint node for this aisle segment in the warehouse graph.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length or clearing cost of this aisle segment (for example, meters of corridor to keep clear). This weight is added to the total cleared distance if the segment is selected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct platforms and boardwalk junctions on the reserve map; each represents a node that can be part of the restored continuous trail.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of individual footbridge or boardwalk segments listed as repairable pieces; each is an edge you may choose to fix or leave unrepaired.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of observation platforms (key viewing points) that must be included and connected by the restored continuous route; every platform named here must lie on the final connected subgraph.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a repairable segment: the identifier of the first platform or junction that this footbridge/boardwalk piece connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the repairable segment: the identifier of the second platform or junction that this footbridge/boardwalk piece connects.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost (or effort score) to restore this specific footbridge or boardwalk segment; include the segment's entire cost if you choose to repair it (segments are either repaired in full or not at all).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct network nodes on the campus map (every building or network junction represented in the graph), including both the key academic buildings that must be connected and any additional buildings that can act as intermediate/Steiner nodes.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate fiber links (graph edges) between campus nodes shown on the map. Each edge represents a physical cable segment that can be activated; the count includes every listed link regardless of whether it will be turned on in the final plan.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of terminal nodes corresponding to the key academic buildings that must be included in the activated network. Every identifier in this list must be connected to the same live subnetwork in the final selection of activated links.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node identifier for this candidate fiber link (e.g., building or junction ID). Used together with 'v' to specify which two campus locations this cable segment would connect if activated.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node identifier for this candidate fiber link (the second building or junction ID). The pair (u, v) defines the specific campus cable segment that can be switched on as part of the solution.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of the cable segment between u and v, representing the contribution to total activated cable length if this link is turned on. This numeric value is used directly in the objective to minimize the sum of lengths of all activated links (units as given on the map).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct locations in the delivery map (all flagship stores plus regional hubs). This is the number of nodes the solver may use when selecting lanes to keep.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate delivery lanes (links) between locations shown on the map. Each lane is a potential edge the solver can choose to keep open.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of locations that are flagship stores which must remain connected in the final pruned network. No item in this list may be left disconnected from the others.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or index) of one endpoint location for this delivery lane — a store or regional hub at one end of the link.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or index) of the other endpoint location for this delivery lane — the store or regional hub at the other end of the link.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (travel distance or cost) of the delivery lane between the two endpoints. The solver sums chosen lanes' distances to evaluate the total kept-open network length.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations represented as graph nodes (includes all treatment plants and existing valve stations that can serve as junctions). This counts every site that appears as an endpoint of available pipe segments.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate pipe segments (edges) that could be installed between locations. Each corresponds to a specific possible piece of pipe with a given length.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers that are treatment plants which must be connected in the final installed pipeline network. These are the terminals the solution must span; valve stations are not mandatory unless needed to connect them.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location for this candidate pipe segment; this is either a treatment plant or an existing valve station where the pipe would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location for this candidate pipe segment; this is either a treatment plant or an existing valve station where the pipe would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length of this candidate pipe segment (the installation cost measured in pipeline length units). The objective is the sum of lengths of chosen segments; segments must not be double-counted.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of locations on the map: every landmark tree and every lamp post that can be used as a connector. These are the graph nodes among which wiring runs may be placed.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate wiring runs between nodes. Each run is an optional edge that can be installed to carry power between two nodes; the solver chooses some subset of these to form the powered circuit.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of node identifiers corresponding to the landmark trees that must all be included in a single continuous powered circuit. Lamp posts listed among nodes are not in this list unless they are also a required tree.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node identifier for a candidate wiring run. This refers to either a landmark tree or a lamp post where the run can be connected.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node identifier for the same candidate wiring run. Together with run_endpoint_u it specifies which two locations this possible piece of wiring would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of the candidate wiring run between the two endpoints, representing how much wiring is required if that run is installed. The goal is to minimize the sum of chosen run_length values while connecting all required_landmark_trees.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct street intersections or endpoints in the subdivision map (i.e., graph nodes). This tells you how many intersection points exist where preserved road segments can meet.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of individual road segments in the map (i.e., graph edges). Each segment is a candidate to keep open or close; the STP chooses a subset of these to preserve.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of nodes that correspond to fire hydrant locations which must be connected by the preserved street network. Every hydrant node must lie in the same kept subnetwork so crews can reach each hydrant.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint intersection/node of this road segment. Used with 'segment_endpoint_b' to identify which two intersections the road connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint intersection/node of this road segment. Together with 'segment_endpoint_a' it defines the specific minor or major street link considered for preservation.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of the road segment between the two endpoints, expressed in the same distance units used to judge total kept road length. The STP minimizes the sum of these values for preserved segments.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct pavement nodes in the airport layout graph (every gate location, taxiway junction, and apron reference point). This is the count of vertices that clearing decisions may reference.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate pavement segments (edges) between nodes. Each represents a contiguous taxiway or apron stretch that can be cleared; the planner chooses some of these to form the cleared network.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to the assigned gates that must lie on the cleared network. The chosen cleared segments must connect all these gates so they are mutually reachable (other apron/taxiway nodes may be included as Steiner intermediates).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint node of this pavement segment (one end of the taxiway/apron stretch). Matches one of the node IDs counted in total_pavement_nodes.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint node of this pavement segment (the opposite end of the taxiway/apron stretch). The segment connects segment_endpoint_a and segment_endpoint_b in the cleared network if chosen.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (cost) in meters of this pavement segment that must be cleared if the segment is included. The objective is to minimize the sum of clear_length_meters over all chosen segments while connecting all assigned_gates.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of landscape patches (nodes) in the map — includes both protected habitats and unprotected patches that can serve as stepping stones. Nodes are the locations between which restoration corridors could be placed.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate restoration strips (edges) connecting pairs of patches. Each edge represents a possible corridor that can be restored to allow movement between its two endpoint patches.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of nodes that are protected habitats and must be connected by the restored corridor network. These are the required terminals in the Steiner-tree formulation; unlisted nodes may be used as intermediate (Steiner) stepping-stone patches.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint patch of this candidate corridor (node identifier). Together with 'v' it defines which two patches the corridor would connect if restored.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint patch of this candidate corridor (node identifier). Corridors are undirected links between patch_a and patch_b allowing movement both directions when restored.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Restoration cost for this corridor, expressed as the area that must be restored to open the strip. When selecting a set of corridors, the solver sums the restoration_area of chosen edges (shared sections counted once) to minimize total restored area.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct support junctions (nodes) in the rigging map — this counts installation mounting points plus any optional intermediate support points that can act as Steiner nodes.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate truss segments (edges) shown on the map — each represents a straight piece that can be assembled between two junctions.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node IDs corresponding to the highlighted artworks/installations that must be included in the same connected truss structure; these are the terminals the final assembly must span.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint junction ID for this candidate truss segment — a labeled support or installation mounting point on the map.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint junction ID for the candidate truss segment — a second support or mounting point the piece would connect to.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (cost) of the truss segment between junction_u and junction_v, expressed in the map's linear units (e.g., meters); use this to sum total truss used and minimize overall length.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct fence junctions or gate posts (nodes) available in the plan. Each node represents a corner/post where fence sections can meet or where a garden connects into the fenced network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of candidate decorative fence sections (edges) that could be installed. Each item corresponds to a potential link between two gate posts; selecting a subset of these builds the continuous fenced network.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of node identifiers that represent the agreed gardens which must be part of the single connected fenced system. Every node in this list must be connected (via chosen sections) to the rest of the chosen subnetwork.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node identifier of this candidate fence section — a specific gate post or corner where the section can be attached.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node identifier of this candidate fence section — the opposite gate post or corner for this section.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The physical length (cost) of this fence section (e.g., in meters). The solver minimizes the sum of section_length for all installed sections; sections are undirected and counted only once if installed.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of nodes in the city's street graph: this counts all intersections and locations represented as nodes, including both the municipal buildings that must be connected and any intermediate junctions available for routing.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of street segments available for trenching in the graph: each edge is a candidate street where fiber can be laid and has an associated trench length/cost.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to the municipal/public buildings that must be included in the final connected trench network; every listed building must lie on the chosen connected set of streets.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint intersection (node identifier) of a street segment: represents one junction or location the street connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint intersection (node identifier) of the same street segment: together with 'intersection_u' identifies which two intersections the street runs between.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Trenching length or cost for that street segment (typically in meters or the units used here): if this street is chosen, its length contributes this amount to the total trench length to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct survey points on the site plan (every labeled location that can be a pipe endpoint or junction, including marked garden beds and potential Steiner/junction points).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of possible direct pipe runs shown on the plan (each candidate connection between two site points that you could choose to install).

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of node identifiers that correspond to the homeowner's marked garden beds; every node in this list must be connected by the installed piping network.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint of a candidate pipe segment (refers to one of the site points).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint of the candidate pipe segment (the segment connects this point to endpoint_a).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of that candidate pipe segment measured in the plan's distance units (this is what adds to the total pipe run if the segment is installed).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct map locations (clearings or junctions) represented as nodes. These are points where footpaths meet and which may act as intermediate (Steiner) nodes when connecting trailheads.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available footpath segments on the map. Each represents a candidate path that can be hardened; the solver chooses a subset of these so all required trailheads become connected.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to the trailheads that must be joined by the paved network. None of these may be omitted; the chosen set of paths must produce a connected subnetwork that spans all these trailheads.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint of this footpath segment: the clearing or junction at one end of the path. Used with 'endpoint_v' to specify which two locations the segment connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint of this footpath segment: the clearing or junction at the opposite end of the path. Together with 'endpoint_u' it defines the undirected segment that can be paved.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The paving length (weight) of this footpath segment. When a segment is included in the recommendation its length is added once to the total paving length used to evaluate solution quality.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations (rooms, corridors, or junction points) on the museum map that are represented as graph nodes. This is the count of all possible places where wiring endpoints or junctions can sit.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate wiring runs (possible cable segments) between locations shown on the map. Each run is a single edge that could be installed if it helps connect the display cases.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of nodes that correspond to display cases which must be included in the final security loop. Every entry here is a terminal that the chosen wiring subgraph must span.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location of this candidate wiring run (node identifier for one room or junction).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location of this candidate wiring run (node identifier for the adjacent room or junction).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (cost) of this wiring run, i.e., the amount of cable required to install this segment. The solver should sum these lengths for all selected runs to get the total cable length to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct graph nodes in the office plan — includes offices, workstation locations, and hallway junctions. Use this to know how many locations the layout contains.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available corridor/hallway segments in the layout. Each corresponds to one undirected edge representing a possible path to run cable between two nodes.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to the critical desks/workstations that must be connected by the final wired network. These nodes are required to be included in the connected subgraph; other nodes may be used as intermediate (Steiner) rooms.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint of a corridor (a room or hallway junction). Combined with 'v' this defines an undirected corridor you can choose to run cable through.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint of the corridor (a room or hallway junction). Together with 'u' defines the corridor connecting these two locations.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length of the corridor in units of cable (e.g., meters). If this corridor is selected in the plan, its length is added once to the total cable length to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the campsite map (includes all campsites and common areas that can be used as link points). Each location is a graph node.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential trail segments between locations. Each edge represents a possible path that could be cleared and marked, with an associated length/cost.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to the campsites that must be connected by the final route. Commons (non-terminals) may be used as intermediate link points but every listed campsite must be included.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location for this potential trail segment (a campsite or a common area).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location for this potential trail segment (a campsite or a common area).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length or cost to clear and mark the trail between endpoint_a and endpoint_b (same distance unit for all edges). The solver minimizes the total of chosen trail_length values while connecting all required campsites.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct physical locations (nodes) on the map, including both substations that must be connected and optional intermediate junctions that may act as Steiner nodes. Node identifiers referenced elsewhere correspond to these locations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of potential distribution lines (edges) that could be built. Each candidate line links two nodes and has an associated material cost/length; the solver chooses a subset of these lines to build.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers that represent substations which must all be included in the final network. The chosen set of lines must connect all these substations into one continuous grid; other junctions may be used to achieve lower total cost.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint of a candidate distribution line; this refers to a specific node on the map (either a substation or an intermediate junction).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint of the candidate distribution line; together with endpoint_node_a it defines the physical line that could be built between the two nodes.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Material cost or length to build the distribution line between the two endpoints. The coordinator sums these costs for selected lines; each listed line can be built once and, when built, connects both endpoints (undirected). Lower total is better.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct physical locations represented on the map (classrooms, hallway intersections, lobbies or other public spaces). Each such location is a graph node that can be an endpoint of corridors or act as a Steiner link.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of direct connections between locations (hallway segments, short passageways, or designated links through public spaces). Each edge represents a contiguous corridor segment whose widening/renovation length contributes to the plan cost.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to the classrooms that must be included in the single accessible corridor system (the program’s target classrooms). The final selected subnetwork must connect all these terminal nodes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location for this corridor segment (a classroom, intersection, lobby, or other public space). Matches a node ID from the global node set.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location for this corridor segment. Together with 'endpoint_a' defines the specific hallway or link that can be chosen for widening.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Linear length (e.g., meters) or equivalent renovation measure for that corridor segment between the two endpoints. When selecting edges, sum these weights to compare total renovation length; each chosen corridor is counted once in the total.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of physical connection points in the neighborhood layout (every lamppost pole and junction box represented as a graph node).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct wiring segments available between poles/junctions (each represents a potential cable run / graph edge).

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers that correspond to the community squares whose lamppost circuits must all be included in the single connected lighting network (these are the terminals).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint pole or junction for this potential wiring segment (one end of the edge).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint pole or junction for this potential wiring segment (the other end of the edge).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length of the wiring needed to connect pole_u and pole_v (the edge weight); used to sum total cable deployed in the plan.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct points on the countryside map — every crossroads and every pickup location — that appear as nodes in the road network. This is the number of nodes the planner can reference when selecting roads.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of rural road segments listed in the instance. Each segment connects two nodes and is a candidate for inclusion in the planner’s route network; this is the size of that candidate list.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of node identifiers that are pickup locations which must be connected. The chosen set of roads must produce one continuous drivable network that spans all these required pickup sites (other crossroads may be used as Steiner nodes).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint of a specific rural road segment (either a crossroads or a pickup location). Used together with 'road_endpoint_b' to specify which two map points that road connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint of the road segment corresponding to 'road_endpoint_a'. The pair (road_endpoint_a, road_endpoint_b) specifies a single undirected road between two map points.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (weight) of the road segment between the two endpoints, measured in miles (or consistent distance units). When evaluating plans, include each selected road’s length once; the planner aims to minimize the sum of these values while connecting all required pickup sites.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the building map (this counts every room and every service/utility space that could host a duct junction or pass-through).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of possible duct segments on the map — each represents a physical piece of ductwork that could be installed between two locations.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of the room node identifiers that must be served by the ventilation system; every entry here is a required room that the chosen duct layout must connect into the single continuous network.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint location of a candidate duct segment (one room or service space). Used together with 'v' to specify which two locations the segment would join.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint location of the candidate duct segment (one room or service space). The segment connects this location to 'u'. Segments are undirected links between locations.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (cost) of that duct segment, measured in feet of duct to install. The objective is to minimize the sum of these lengths for the selected segments while connecting all required rooms.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of habitat patches (graph nodes) in the area being considered. Use this to understand the size of the landscape graph from which corridors can be chosen.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate corridors (graph edges) between patches. Each corridor is a potential link that can be maintained; this counts every unique corridor once.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of the monitored habitat patches that must be connected in the final maintained network. Every patch listed here must be included in the connected subgraph returned.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint habitat patch of this candidate corridor. Identifies one of the two patches that the corridor would directly connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint habitat patch of this candidate corridor. Together with patch_endpoint_a, it defines the two patches joined by this corridor.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (cost) of the corridor between the two endpoint patches, representing fencing/clearing required. When selecting corridors, sum these values; each corridor is counted once toward the total cost.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct backroom areas or zones in the store plan (each node is a room, storage area, or service point that can be used in the route).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate backroom passages or corridors between zones (each edge is a possible corridor that can be opened).

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of designated store areas (node identifiers) that must be included on the single connected service circuit; these are the terminals the chosen passages must span.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one end of a candidate passage — the first backroom zone connected by this corridor.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other end of the candidate passage — the second backroom zone connected by this corridor.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length or cost of opening this passage (e.g., meters of corridor); contributes to the total length that the planner seeks to minimize if the passage is included.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct backstage locations in the venue layout (this includes all staging zones and any other backstage areas that can be used as intermediate spots).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential platform connector runs available in the layout (each corresponds to an edge between two backstage locations).

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers for the staging zones that must be joined into a single connected backstage network; every entry here must be included in the final connector plan.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint backstage location for this potential connector run (matches a node id from the venue layout).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint backstage location for this potential connector run (matches a node id from the venue layout).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of this connector run between the two endpoints; when choosing a plan, sum these lengths for every installed connector.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations marked on the park layout (each location is a bench site or a clearing that can serve as an intermediate tie‑in). This counts every node that can be used when building the promenade.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate short paths shown between locations on the layout. Each represents an available connection (possible segment of promenade) that can be chosen or omitted when forming the final route.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of location identifiers that correspond to picnic groves (the required benches/grove sites). Every identifier here must be spanned by the chosen promenade so that all groves are connected in a single continuous route.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint of a candidate short path (a bench or a clearing). Used with 'v' to specify which two locations that path would join.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint of a candidate short path (a bench or a clearing). Together with 'u' it defines the two locations connected by this potential promenade segment.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length of this candidate short path (edge) — the cost added to the promenade if this connection is chosen. The solver minimizes the sum of these lengths while ensuring all picnic_groves are connected (clearings may be used as intermediate nodes).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct network locations in the data-center layout (each node is a rack, patch point, or junction that fiber trunks can connect through). This tells the solver how many nodes are in the graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available fiber trunk links in the layout. Each edge corresponds to a candidate trunk that can be turned on or left off when building the connected fabric.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers that are the critical racks which must be connected in the final active fabric. The solution must ensure these nodes are spanned (connected) possibly via other non‑terminal nodes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint of a candidate fiber trunk (an endpoint node id corresponding to a rack or patch point). Used together with 'v' to specify the link.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint of the candidate fiber trunk (a rack or patch point). The pair (endpoint_node_a, endpoint_node_b) defines a trunk link available for activation.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Physical length (cost) of the corresponding trunk between the two endpoints, expressed in meters (or consistent length units). The solver sums these weights for activated trunks and seeks the minimum total length connecting all critical racks.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct pedestrian locations on the map (intersections, plazas, building entrances, or other nodes). This is the count of graph nodes from which sidewalks and side‑street segments connect.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct pedestrian links (sidewalk stretches, side‑street segments, or plaza walkways) represented as edges in the map. Each edge is a single contiguous pavement segment that can be cleared as a unit.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of node identifiers corresponding to emergency shelters that must be included in the single continuous cleared pedestrian route. All these nodes must be connected by the chosen cleared segments; other nodes may serve as intermediate (Steiner) connectors.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint of a sidewalk/street/plaza segment (an intersection, plaza point, or other node). Together with 'v' it defines which two locations the segment connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint of the sidewalk/street/plaza segment. The segment is the undirected link between 'u' and 'v' that can be cleared to contribute to the continuous route.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of that sidewalk/street/plaza segment, expressed in units of pavement length (e.g., meters). If the segment is chosen for clearing it adds this length once to the total cleared distance the planner seeks to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of nodes in the wiring model: each node represents either an interactive station or an intermediate gallery space/room that cables may pass through. This is the number of distinct locations available for placing connectors or routing lines.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available undirected connector segments (edges) in the layout. Each edge is a potential direct link between two nodes (rooms or stations) that can be installed; this count is the number of such candidate links provided in the layout.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of node identifiers that correspond to interactive stations which must be joined into a single connected visitor circuit. These nodes are required endpoints that the chosen installed connectors must span.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node identifier for this potential connector segment — representing either an interactive station or a gallery space at one end of the link.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node identifier for this potential connector segment — the location at the opposite end of the link from endpoint_node_a.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The installation length (cost) of the connector between endpoint_node_a and endpoint_node_b, expressed in the same distance units used for scoring (e.g., meters). When selecting connectors, the total score is the sum of these lengths for chosen edges.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of intersections on the map (all nodes in the street network). This counts every intersection that could be a hub or a possible junction for paved streets.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of street segments shown as paving candidates (each edge in the graph). Each represents a possible street to pave between two intersections.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of intersections that are neighborhood hubs which must be connected by the paved network. Every hub in this list must lie on the chosen paved subnetwork.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint intersection of this street segment. Together with 'intersection_b' identifies which two intersections the candidate street connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint intersection of this street segment. The pair (intersection_a, intersection_b) is the street you may choose to pave.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (paving cost) of this street segment. If you decide to pave this street it contributes this amount to the total paving length; each chosen street counts once regardless of direction.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations considered on the festival map (includes stages, vendor areas, existing junctions and any temporary link points that may be used). This is the count of nodes in the walkway planning graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate walkway segments on the map. Each corresponds to a possible path between two locations that can be built at a listed construction cost.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to every stage and vendor area that must be joined by the final network. These are the spots the chosen walkways must span; temporary link points are not listed here unless they are required spots.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location of this candidate walkway (node index for a stage, vendor area, junction, or potential temporary link point).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location of this candidate walkway (the node at the opposite end of the segment).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Construction cost (weight) to build this walkway segment between the two endpoints. Costs are additive and the objective is to minimize the total cost of the selected segments that connect all required spots.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations shown on the building map (every office, intermediate closet, or junction is a node in the graph). This is the size of the node set you may use when selecting cable segments.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate fiber cable runs depicted on the map (each is an available edge between two locations that can be activated).

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to the offices that must be connected together in a single continuous network. These are mandatory terminals; every listed office must be part of the final activated subnetwork.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location for a given cable segment (may be an office, closet, or junction).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location for the cable segment (may be an office, closet, or junction).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length of that cable segment (the cost to activate this run). Use the same distance units as on the provided map; the solver should sum these values to compare layouts and minimize the total activated cable length.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct towers in the planning graph (includes every required cell site and every optional relay tower). This is the count of nodes a solver will consider when choosing hops.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate microwave hops (edges) available between towers. Each represents a potential activated link that can be used to build the backbone.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to required cell sites that must all be included and connected in the final backbone. These nodes cannot be omitted; relay towers may be used but are not listed here.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint tower for this candidate microwave hop. Together with endpoint_v defines which two towers this potential link would connect if activated.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint tower for this candidate microwave hop. The pair (endpoint_u, endpoint_v) is the undirected link between two towers.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Activation cost (weight) of this microwave hop between the two endpoints. When a plan activates this hop its cost contributes to the total backbone cost; duplicate activations do not add extra cost.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the museum map (every exhibit hall and every foyer/connector). These are the graph nodes the curator may use when planning which corridors to open.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of corridor options (edges) shown on the map that could be opened between rooms. Each corresponds to a potential passage the curator can choose to include in the visitor route.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers that are exhibit halls which must be connected into a single continuous visitor path. Foyers or other non-listed rooms can be used as intermediate connectors but are not required themselves.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one room at an end of a corridor option (one endpoint of the passage). This is a room id used to specify the corridor's endpoints on the museum map.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other room at the opposite end of the corridor option. Together with endpoint_room_a it defines which two rooms the corridor would connect if opened.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (or cost) of opening that corridor between endpoint_room_a and endpoint_room_b. The curator sums these values for every opened corridor and aims to minimize that total while ensuring all required exhibit halls are connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations on the campus map (this counts every academic building and every plaza or junction point that can be used as a connector).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate pedestrian connections (bridges or walkways) shown on the diagram that you may choose to construct.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of terminal nodes that must be included in the final network — specifically the academic buildings (lecture halls, labs, etc.) that must be connected; plazas are not required but may be used as intermediate connectors.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a candidate pedestrian connection; this is the identifier for a site (either an academic building or a plaza/junction).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the candidate pedestrian connection; together with endpoint_a it defines which two sites the walkway or bridge would link.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of the candidate connection between the two endpoints, expressed in the campus distance unit (e.g., meters). The objective is to choose connections whose summed lengths are minimal while connecting all required academic buildings.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct locations considered in the layout: this includes all parking clusters (terminals) and any candidate intermediate junction-box positions (Steiner nodes) that can be used when planning cable runs.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential interconnection options (edges) between locations. Each candidate link represents a possible cable run between two locations that you may choose to install.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node IDs that are parking clusters which must be included in the final connected charging network. These are the terminals that the chosen links must span; other nodes may be used as intermediate junctions but are not required themselves.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint of this candidate cable run. This endpoint may be a parking cluster (terminal) or a potential junction-box location (Steiner node).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint of this candidate cable run. Together with the 'link_endpoint_a' it defines the two locations that would be connected if this link is installed.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The weight assigned to this candidate link: the length of cable (or equivalent cost) required to install the connection between the two endpoints. When computing total network cost, sum the w values for the chosen links (count each installed link once).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of nodes on the map (every shelter location and every crossroads/intersection that crews could clear through).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of blocked road segments shown on the map (each is a candidate street crews could clear to connect nodes).

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers that are shelters and must be connected by cleared roads in the final usable network (these cannot be omitted).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node identifier of a blocked road segment (could be a shelter or a crossroads); crews can clear this segment to connect node_u with node_v.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node identifier of the blocked road segment (could be a shelter or a crossroads); paired with node_u to describe a specific street segment.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length in meters of the blocked road segment between node_u and node_v — the cost (meters to clear) incurred if crews reopen that segment; the objective is to minimize the sum of chosen w values.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct points on the resort map (every lodge, slope access point, and any intermediate transfer/ junction point). This counts all nodes that may appear in the network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of possible transport links on the map (each lift or connector between two stations). This is the number of candidate tracks that can be switched on.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of station identifiers that must be included and interconnected in the operated network (all lodges and slopes that must remain reachable). These are the mandatory endpoints the plan must span.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint station for a given lift or connector (refers to a node on the resort map).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint station for the same lift or connector (the node at the opposite end of this track).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Operational length (cost) of that lift or connector — the amount added to the total operated track length if this edge is switched on. The solver sums these values for chosen tracks.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct garden sites in the plan (includes seating areas and any extra junctions/steiner points). This is the graph node count for the backyard layout.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate hedge or path segments available to plant between garden sites (the graph's edge count). Each represents a potential planted link you may choose.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to the seating areas (benches/tables) that must be joined by a single continuous planted walkway — these are the terminals that the final layout must span.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint garden site for this candidate hedge/path segment; refers to a node ID among the total_junctions.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint garden site for this candidate hedge/path segment; pairs with endpoint_u to define the link between two node IDs.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Planting length of this hedge/path segment in meters (the cost contributed if this link is chosen). The goal is minimizing the sum of chosen segment_length_m values while connecting all seating_areas.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct locations on the campus map that can be used in the cable plan — this includes wireless access clusters (terminals), hardware rooms, and any other junction points represented as nodes.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of possible cable segments (graph edges) shown on the map that can be installed between pairs of locations.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list (by node identifiers) of locations that are wireless access clusters which must be included in the single connected backbone; these are the required terminals that the cable selection must span.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location for this candidate cable segment — may be a wireless cluster, a hardware room, or another junction point.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location for this candidate cable segment — may be a wireless cluster, a hardware room, or another junction point.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The physical length (or cost) of this cable segment in meters (or consistent distance units); when building the backbone, the sum of the chosen segments' lengths is the quantity to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of lamp posts (nodes) in the neighborhood diagram — this counts every pole that could be used, including those at plazas and any spare posts that can act as Steiner nodes.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential wiring segments shown on the diagram — each segment is a possible undirected connection between two lamp posts that can be wired, counted once.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of lamp posts that are at plazas and therefore must be included in the final illuminated circuit (the required terminals that must be connected).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint lamp-post identifier for this potential wiring segment (node label). Together with 'endpoint_post_b' it defines which two posts this segment would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint lamp-post identifier for this potential wiring segment (node label). Segments are undirected: the order of endpoints does not matter.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of wiring required to connect the two posts identified by this segment — a numeric measure (e.g., meters) that contributes to the total wire length when the segment is chosen.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct dock junctions, piers, and end points in the marina layout. Each node represents a physical point where one or more dock segments meet; some of these nodes are berthing zones that must be connected, others are spare piers that may be used as intermediate connectors.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of individual dock segments (walkway sections) that can be retrofitted. Each segment connects two junction points and has an associated retrofit length; selecting segments builds the continuous boardwalk covering required berthing zones.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node identifiers corresponding to berthing zones that must be connected by the retrofitted boardwalk. These terminal nodes are mandatory endpoints of the final connected subgraph; spare piers not listed here may be used as Steiner (intermediate) nodes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint junction for a specific dock segment. Together with the other endpoint this defines which two physical points the segment connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint junction for the dock segment. The pair (segment_endpoint_a, segment_endpoint_b) specifies the two nodes joined by this walkable dock section.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Retrofit length (cost) of this dock segment, expressed in the same linear units used to evaluate total decking to renovate. If this segment is chosen in the plan, its length is added to the total walkway length to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct junctions or endpoints on the map (all graph nodes). This counts every intersection or labeled location, including both donation drop points and other nearby junctions that can serve as Steiner connectors.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of existing footpath segments (graph edges) shown on the map. Each segment is a candidate for repair; selecting a segment means repairing that path and incurring its repair distance once.

global_fields.name: terminals
global_fields.scenario_description: List of node IDs that are donation drop points which must be connected in the repaired network. The chosen set of repaired segments must form a connected subgraph that includes every listed donation drop point.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node ID of a particular footpath segment — the junction or location at one end of this candidate repair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node ID of the same footpath segment — the junction or location at the opposite end of this candidate repair.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (repair distance) of the footpath segment between the two endpoints u and v, in the map's distance units. If this segment is included in the plan, this value contributes once to the total repair distance to minimize.
